# Audit Log  
Track every administrative action in your workspace. Available on the Enterprise plan.

## What is logged  
- User invitations, role changes, removals
- Workflow create/update/delete
- Integration connections, disconnections
- API key creation and deletion
- Settings changes (SSO config, IP allowlist, etc.)
- Billing events  
Workflow runs and integration data flow are not in the audit log; see Run logs for those.

## Accessing the log  
**Settings → Audit Log**. Each entry includes:  
- Timestamp (UTC)
- Actor (user or API key)
- Action (e.g., `workflow.update`)
- Target (the resource affected)
- IP address and user agent

## Searching and filtering  
Filter by date range, actor, action type, or target. Free-text search matches across all fields.

## Retention  
Audit log entries are retained for **365 days**.

## Export  
Export the audit log to CSV or JSON for compliance or external SIEM ingestion. Exports are generated asynchronously and emailed when ready.

## SIEM streaming  
For real-time SIEM integration, configure a webhook destination in **Settings → Audit Log → Stream**. Events are delivered within 60 seconds of occurrence.

# IP Allowlist  
Restrict workspace access to specific IP ranges. Available on the Enterprise plan.

## How it works  
When IP allowlisting is enabled, Helix rejects any request — UI login, API call, or webhook — that originates from outside the allowed CIDR ranges.

## Configuring  
**Settings → Security → IP Allowlist**  
- Add CIDR blocks (IPv4 or IPv6)
- Maximum **50 CIDR ranges** per workspace
- Toggle **Enforce** to activate

## What is restricted  
- Web app login
- API requests
- Webhook delivery (inbound) — your webhook senders must be in the allowlist
- SAML SSO endpoints

## What is NOT restricted  
- Outbound webhooks from Helix to your services (Helix's egress IPs are documented separately)
- Status page access
- Marketing site

## Best practices  
**Allowlist your office VPN** rather than individual IPs. VPN ranges are more stable than individual user IPs.  
**Allowlist webhook senders explicitly**. If you trigger workflows from third-party services, add their documented webhook IP ranges.  
**Do not lock yourself out**. Always include an emergency CIDR (e.g., a backup VPN) in case the primary allowlist becomes unreachable.

## Recovery  
If you accidentally lock yourself out, contact support@helix.io from the email of any Owner or Admin. We can disable enforcement after identity verification.

# Roles and Permissions  
Helix uses role-based access control. Every user in a workspace has exactly one role.

## Available roles  
- **Owner**
- **Admin**
- **Editor**
- **Viewer**

## What each role can do  
| Capability | Owner | Admin | Editor | Viewer |
|------------|-------|-------|--------|--------|
| View workflows | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Run workflows manually | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |  |
| Create / edit workflows | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |  |
| Manage integrations | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |  |
| Invite users | ✓ | ✓ |  |  |
| Manage roles | ✓ | ✓ |  |  |
| Manage billing | ✓ |  |  |  |
| Delete workspace | ✓ |  |  |  |
| Transfer ownership | ✓ |  |  |  |

## The Owner role  
Each workspace has exactly one Owner. The Owner has all permissions including billing and workspace deletion. To change Owner, the current Owner must transfer ownership in **Settings → Workspace → Transfer ownership**.

## Changing a user's role  
Admins and Owners can change roles in **Settings → Team**. Click a user's row to see role options.

## Custom roles  
Custom roles are available on Enterprise plans. Contact your account team to define roles with specific scopes.

# SCIM Provisioning  
Automate user lifecycle with SCIM 2.0. Available on the Enterprise plan.

## What SCIM does  
SCIM lets your identity provider automatically:  
- Create Helix users when added to your IdP.
- Update user attributes (name, email, role) on changes.
- Deactivate users when removed from your IdP.

## Supported providers  
- Okta
- Azure AD / Microsoft Entra
- OneLogin
- JumpCloud
- Any SCIM 2.0-compliant provider

## Setup  
1. Enable SCIM in **Settings → Security → SCIM**.
2. Helix issues a SCIM token. Copy it.
3. In your IdP, create a SCIM provisioning app pointing to:
- **SCIM URL**: `https://api.helix.io/v2/scim/v2`
- **Token**: the token from step 2.
4. Map your IdP attributes to Helix attributes (email, displayName, role).
5. Enable provisioning and select which IdP groups sync to Helix.

## Role mapping  
By default, all SCIM-provisioned users get the **Editor** role. To map roles, set the SCIM `userType` attribute to one of: `Owner`, `Admin`, `Editor`, `Viewer`. The Owner role cannot be assigned via SCIM — use the Helix UI for that.

## Deactivation  
When SCIM marks a user as inactive, Helix:  
1. Revokes all active sessions.
2. Disables API keys created by that user (within 1 hour).
3. Marks the user as deactivated but does not delete their data.  
To fully delete a user, an Admin must do so from the Helix UI.

# Security Settings  
Workspace-wide security controls available under **Settings → Security**.

## Password requirements  
For non-SSO users, configure password policy:  
- Minimum length: 8 to 32 characters
- Require uppercase, lowercase, numbers, special characters
- Disallow recent passwords (last 5)
- Maximum age: 30 to 365 days

## Session timeout  
Configure how long a session lasts before re-authentication is required:  
- Web sessions: 1 hour to 30 days
- API keys do not expire automatically; rotate manually

## Two-factor authentication  
Enforce 2FA for all users via **Require 2FA**. Users without 2FA configured will be prompted to set it up on next login.  
Supported 2FA methods:
- TOTP apps (Authy, Google Authenticator, 1Password)
- WebAuthn / hardware keys (YubiKey, Titan)
- SMS (not recommended; TOTP and WebAuthn are stronger)

## Login monitoring  
The **Login activity** page shows successful and failed login attempts for every user. Filter by user, location, or status.

## Session revocation  
Admins can revoke individual sessions or all sessions for a user under **Team → User → Sessions**. Useful when a user reports a lost device.

# Single Sign-On (SSO)  
SSO via SAML 2.0 is available on the Enterprise plan.

## Supported identity providers  
- Okta
- Azure AD / Microsoft Entra
- Google Workspace
- OneLogin
- Auth0
- Any SAML 2.0-compliant IdP

## Setup steps  
1. Contact your account team to enable SSO for your workspace.
2. In **Settings → Security → SSO**, you'll find the Helix-side SAML metadata.
3. Configure your IdP with this metadata:
- **Entity ID**: provided in settings
- **ACS URL**: provided in settings
- **NameID format**: emailAddress
4. Upload your IdP's metadata XML to Helix.
5. Test with a single user before rolling out to the team.

## Just-in-time provisioning  
When a new user signs in via SSO and doesn't yet have a Helix account, Helix automatically provisions one with the **Editor** role. To change the default role, configure **JIT default role** in security settings.

## Forcing SSO  
To require all users to sign in via SSO (no password fallback), enable **Enforce SSO** in security settings. Existing password-based sessions are invalidated; users must re-authenticate via SSO.

## Service accounts and SSO  
Service accounts (used for API keys) bypass SSO. They authenticate via API key only.

## Common issues  
**"User not found" after SSO redirect**: The IdP is not sending the user's email in the NameID field. Adjust your IdP's NameID format.  
**Loop redirect to IdP**: Browser cookies are blocked. Check third-party cookie settings.

# Teams  
Group users into teams for easier permission management.

## Creating teams  
**Settings → Teams → New team**. Provide a name and an optional description.

## Adding members  
Click a team and use **Add members** to assign users. A user can belong to multiple teams.

## Team-scoped permissions  
Use teams to:  
- Restrict workflow visibility (only members of Team X can see Team X's workflows)
- Restrict connection usage (only members of Team Y can use Team Y's integrations)
- Send team-wide notifications

## Default behavior  
By default, all workflows and connections are workspace-wide visible. Team scoping must be explicitly enabled per resource.

## Team admins  
Each team can have one or more team admins. Team admins can manage team membership but do not gain workspace-level admin permissions.

# User Provisioning  
Add users to your workspace via invitation, SSO, or SCIM.

## Invitation flow  
1. **Settings → Team → Invite users**
2. Enter email addresses (comma-separated for bulk)
3. Choose a role for the invitees
4. Send invitations  
Invitees receive an email with a join link. Links expire after 7 days. To resend, click the user row in **Pending invitations** and select **Resend**.

## SSO auto-provisioning  
If SSO is enabled, new users authenticated by your IdP are auto-provisioned. The default role is Editor; configure under **Settings → Security → SSO**.

## SCIM auto-provisioning  
With SCIM, users in selected IdP groups are automatically provisioned and deprovisioned. See SCIM documentation for setup.

## Bulk invitation via API  
```
POST /v2/users/invite
{
"users": [
{"email": "alice@company.com", "role": "Editor"},
{"email": "bob@company.com", "role": "Viewer"}
]
}
```

## Domain capture  
Enterprise customers can claim email domains so all users with matching emails are auto-provisioned to your workspace on first sign-in. Contact your account team.

# API Versioning  
Helix's API is versioned in the URL path: `https://api.helix.io/v2`.

## Current version  
**v2** is the current stable version.

## Backwards compatibility  
Within a major version, the following changes will not be made:  
- Removing endpoints
- Removing fields from responses
- Adding required fields to requests
- Changing the type of an existing field  
The following changes are considered backwards compatible:  
- Adding new endpoints
- Adding new optional fields to requests
- Adding new fields to responses (your client should ignore unknown fields)
- Adding new error codes (handle unknown codes generically)

## Deprecation policy  
When we deprecate an endpoint or field:  
1. Documentation is updated to mark it deprecated.
2. Responses include a `Deprecation` header.
3. The deprecated feature continues to work for at least 12 months.
4. We send email notices to API key owners 30 days before removal.

## Version history  
- **v2** (current): Released 2023. Adds webhooks, scoped API keys, GraphQL endpoint.
- **v1** (deprecated): Released 2020. Sunset date 2024-12-31.

# API Authentication  
The Helix API uses bearer token authentication.

## Generating API keys  
1. Go to **Settings → API Keys**.
2. Click **Create new key**.
3. Choose **Live** or **Test**.
4. Name the key (for your reference).
5. Copy the key immediately — Helix shows it once and never again.

## Using the key  
Include the key in the `Authorization` header of every request:  
```
Authorization: Bearer hlx_live_a1b2c3d4...
```

## Key permissions  
By default, API keys have full access to your workspace. To restrict a key, configure **Scoped keys** under **Settings → API Keys → Advanced**:  
- `workflows:read`
- `workflows:write`
- `runs:read`
- `runs:trigger`
- `integrations:read`

## Rotating keys  
To rotate:  
1. Generate a new key.
2. Update your applications to use the new key.
3. Once you've verified the new key works, delete the old key.  
Deleted keys cannot be recovered.

## Common authentication errors  
- **Invalid or expired API key** — Returned as 401. The key is missing, malformed, or has been deleted.
- **Insufficient permissions for this resource** — Returned as 403. The key is valid but doesn't have the scope to perform this action.

# API Errors  
Helix uses standard HTTP status codes and returns structured error bodies.

## Error codes  
| Code | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| 400 | Bad request — malformed JSON or missing required fields |
| 401 | Invalid or expired API key |
| 403 | Insufficient permissions for this resource |
| 404 | Resource not found |
| 422 | Validation error — check request body |
| 429 | Rate limit exceeded |
| 500 | Internal server error |
| 503 | Service temporarily unavailable |

## Error body format  
```json
{
"error": {
"type": "validation_error",
"message": "Workflow name must be between 1 and 64 characters",
"field": "name",
"request_id": "req_abc123"
}
}
```  
Always log `request_id` — our support team can use it to investigate issues.

## Retrying  
- 5xx errors should be retried with exponential backoff.
- 429 errors should be retried after the `Retry-After` delay.
- 4xx errors (except 429) should NOT be retried — they indicate a permanent problem with your request.

## Idempotency  
Mutating endpoints support an optional `Idempotency-Key` header. Pass any unique string. Helix will return the same response for repeated requests with the same key, allowing safe retries.

# API Overview  
The Helix API lets you manage workflows, runs, and integrations programmatically.

## Base URL  
All API requests go to:  
```
https://api.helix.io/v2
```

## Authentication  
All requests require an API key in the **Authorization** header:  
```
Authorization: Bearer hlx_live_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx
```

## API key formats  
- **Live keys**: `hlx_live_<32 hex chars>` — affects production resources.
- **Test keys**: `hlx_test_<32 hex chars>` — sandboxed; safe for development.  
Generate API keys from **Settings → API Keys**. Keep keys secret — never commit them to version control.

## Plan requirements  
API access is included on Pro and Enterprise plans. Starter plans do not include API access.

## Versioning  
The current version is **v2**. We maintain backwards compatibility within a major version. Breaking changes will be released as v3 with at least 12 months of overlap.

## Quick start  
```bash
curl https://api.helix.io/v2/workflows \
-H "Authorization: Bearer hlx_live_xxxxxxxx"
```

# Pagination  
Helix uses cursor-based pagination for all list endpoints.

## How it works  
List responses include a `next_cursor` field. To fetch the next page, pass this value as the `cursor` query parameter.  
```json
{
"data": [...],
"next_cursor": "eyJpZCI6Imxhc3RfaXRlbV9pZCJ9",
"has_more": true
}
```  
When `has_more` is `false`, you have reached the end. The `next_cursor` field will be omitted.

## Page size  
Use the `limit` query parameter to control page size. The default is 25 and the maximum is 100.  
```
GET https://api.helix.io/v2/runs?limit=100
```

## Stable ordering  
Pagination is stable: items added or removed during paging will not cause duplicates or skips. Items are ordered by creation time descending unless otherwise documented.

## Common mistake  
Do not infer the cursor from the data. The `next_cursor` is opaque — its format may change. Always use the value returned by the previous response.

# API Rate Limits  
Helix enforces rate limits to ensure platform stability and fair use.

## Limits by plan  
| Plan | Requests per minute |
|------|---------------------|
| Starter | API access not included |
| Pro | **1000** |
| Enterprise | **unlimited** |  
Limits are per-workspace, not per-API-key. All keys in the same workspace share the budget.

## Rate limit headers  
Every API response includes these headers:  
```
X-RateLimit-Limit: 1000
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 847
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1714515600
```  
`X-RateLimit-Reset` is a Unix timestamp indicating when the budget refills.

## When you hit the limit  
Helix returns **429 with Retry-After header**. The Retry-After header indicates how many seconds to wait before retrying.  
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 23
```

## Best practices  
- **Respect Retry-After**: Pause your client when you receive 429 and resume after the indicated delay.
- **Implement exponential backoff**: For repeated 429s, double the wait between retries.
- **Batch where possible**: Some endpoints support bulk operations to reduce request count.
- **Use webhooks instead of polling**: If you're polling for changes, switch to webhooks.

## Exemptions  
Enterprise customers can request a custom rate limit by contacting their account team.

# Runs Endpoint  
Trigger and inspect workflow runs.

## Trigger a run  
```
POST https://api.helix.io/v2/workflows/{workflow_id}/runs
Content-Type: application/json

{
"input": { "any": "json data" }
}
```  
Returns immediately with a `run_id`. The run executes asynchronously.

## Get a run  
```
GET https://api.helix.io/v2/runs/{run_id}
```  
Returns the run's current state including:
- `status`: `pending`, `running`, `succeeded`, `failed`, `cancelled`
- `started_at`, `finished_at`
- `steps`: array of step executions with their inputs and outputs
- `error`: details if the run failed

## List runs  
```
GET https://api.helix.io/v2/runs
```  
Query parameters:
- `workflow_id` (filter by workflow)
- `status` (filter by status)
- `started_after`, `started_before` (ISO 8601 timestamps)
- `limit` (default 25, max 100)
- `cursor` (pagination)

## Cancel a run  
```
POST https://api.helix.io/v2/runs/{run_id}/cancel
```  
Cancels a running execution. Already-completed steps are not rolled back.

## Retention  
Run records are retained for **90 days** on Pro plans and **365 days** on Enterprise plans. Older runs are deleted automatically.

# Official SDKs  
Helix maintains official SDKs for major languages.

## Available SDKs  
- **Python** — `pip install helix-sdk`
- **Node.js** — `npm install @helix/sdk`
- **Go** — `go get github.com/helix/helix-go`
- **Ruby** — `gem install helix-sdk`

## Authentication  
All SDKs accept an API key via constructor or environment variable.

### Python  
```python
from helix import Helix
client = Helix(api_key="hlx_live_xxxxxxxx")
workflows = client.workflows.list()
```

### Node.js  
```javascript
const { Helix } = require('@helix/sdk');
const client = new Helix({ apiKey: 'hlx_live_xxxxxxxx' });
const workflows = await client.workflows.list();
```

## Environment variable  
If `HELIX_API_KEY` is set, you can omit the constructor argument:  
```python
client = Helix()  # reads HELIX_API_KEY
```

## Versioning  
SDK versions follow semver. The major version matches the API version (e.g., SDK 2.x matches API v2).

## Issues and feedback  
Report bugs at github.com/helix/helix-{language}. PRs are welcome.

# Webhooks  
Subscribe to Helix events in your own services.

## Creating a webhook subscription  
```
POST https://api.helix.io/v2/webhooks
{
"url": "https://yourapp.com/helix-webhook",
"events": ["run.succeeded", "run.failed"],
"secret": "your_signing_secret"
}
```

## Available events  
- `workflow.created`
- `workflow.updated`
- `workflow.deleted`
- `run.started`
- `run.succeeded`
- `run.failed`
- `run.cancelled`

## Verifying signatures  
Every webhook delivery includes a **X-Helix-Signature** header containing an **HMAC-SHA256** signature of the body, computed with your subscription's secret.  
To verify in Python:  
```python
import hmac, hashlib
expected = hmac.new(secret.encode(), body, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
if not hmac.compare_digest(expected, received_signature):
raise Exception("Invalid signature")
```

## Delivery and retries  
Helix POSTs the event to your URL with a **30 seconds** timeout. If your endpoint returns 2xx, the delivery is marked successful.  
If your endpoint fails (timeout, 5xx, or non-2xx), Helix retries up to **3** times with exponential backoff.  
After all retries fail, the delivery is marked permanently failed and a notification is sent to the workspace owner.

## Inspecting deliveries  
The **Webhook Logs** page shows every delivery attempt with status code, response body, and timing.

# Workflows Endpoint  
Manage workflows programmatically.

## List workflows  
```
GET https://api.helix.io/v2/workflows
```  
Returns a paginated list of workflows in the workspace.  
Query parameters:
- `limit` (default 25, max 100)
- `cursor` (for pagination)
- `status` (filter by `active` or `inactive`)

## Get a workflow  
```
GET https://api.helix.io/v2/workflows/{workflow_id}
```  
Returns the full workflow definition including all steps.

## Create a workflow  
```
POST https://api.helix.io/v2/workflows
Content-Type: application/json

{
"name": "My new workflow",
"trigger": { "type": "webhook" },
"steps": [...]
}
```  
Returns the created workflow with a generated `workflow_id`.

## Update a workflow  
```
PATCH https://api.helix.io/v2/workflows/{workflow_id}
Content-Type: application/json

{
"name": "Updated name"
}
```  
Updates only the fields included. Supplying a full `steps` array creates a new version.

## Delete a workflow  
```
DELETE https://api.helix.io/v2/workflows/{workflow_id}
```  
Soft-deletes the workflow. Existing runs continue to completion. Hard deletion happens 30 days later.

## Activate / deactivate  
```
POST https://api.helix.io/v2/workflows/{workflow_id}/activate
POST https://api.helix.io/v2/workflows/{workflow_id}/deactivate
```

# Invoices and Receipts  
Access your billing history and receipts under **Settings → Billing**.

## Viewing invoices  
**Settings → Billing → Invoices** lists all past invoices with status (paid, pending, overdue) and amount. Click any invoice to download the PDF.

## Invoice contents  
Each invoice includes:  
- Invoice number and date
- Billing period
- Plan name and seat count
- Line items (subscription, overage charges, add-ons)
- Subtotal, tax, total
- Payment status

## Tax handling  
Helix collects sales tax in jurisdictions where required. Tax is shown as a line item.  
For VAT/GST, provide your VAT/GST number under **Settings → Billing → Tax info**. Reverse-charge applies for B2B customers in eligible jurisdictions.

## Custom invoice fields  
Enterprise customers can add PO numbers, custom remit-to addresses, or custom line item descriptions. Configure these under **Settings → Billing → Invoice customization**.

## Downloading historical invoices  
All invoices are retained indefinitely. Download in bulk via **Settings → Billing → Export all**.

# Payment Methods  
Helix accepts credit cards, ACH transfer, and (Enterprise only) wire transfer or invoice billing.

## Adding a payment method  
**Settings → Billing → Payment methods → Add new**.  
We accept:
- Visa, Mastercard, American Express, Discover
- ACH (US bank accounts)
- Wire transfer (Enterprise)

## Default payment method  
If you have multiple payment methods, designate one as default. Subscription charges use the default; you can override per invoice.

## Updating cards  
To update a card, add the new card and delete the old one. We do not support direct edits.

## Failed payments  
If a charge fails, Helix retries automatically:  
- 1st retry: 1 day later
- 2nd retry: 3 days later
- 3rd retry: 7 days later  
After all retries fail, your account is downgraded to a read-only state. You can still view runs but cannot create or trigger new ones.

## Invoice billing (Enterprise)  
Enterprise contracts can be billed via invoice with NET-30 or NET-60 terms. Invoices are sent monthly or annually depending on contract.

# Changing Plans  
Upgrade, downgrade, or cancel your plan from **Settings → Billing → Plan**.

## Upgrades  
Upgrades take effect immediately. Helix prorates the difference between your old and new plan for the remainder of the current billing period.  
After upgrade:
- New plan limits apply right away.
- New features (integrations, API access, etc.) are unlocked.
- Existing data and workflows are preserved.

## Downgrades  
Downgrades take effect at the end of the current billing period. Until then, you keep your current plan's features.  
When the downgrade activates:
- New plan limits apply.
- Features no longer in your plan become unavailable. Workflows that depend on disabled features will fail.
- We do not delete data when you downgrade.

## Cancellation  
Cancellation takes effect at the end of the current billing period. You retain full access until then.  
After cancellation:
- Workflows continue running through the end of the period.
- After the period ends, workflows are paused and the workspace is read-only for 90 days.
- After 90 days, the workspace is permanently deleted unless you reactivate.

## Annual to monthly  
Switching from annual to monthly takes effect at your next renewal. We do not refund prorated amounts on annual plans.

## Refunds  
We do not offer refunds for partial months. If you cancel mid-cycle, you continue to have access until the period ends.

# Plans and Pricing  
Helix offers three plans: Starter, Pro, and Enterprise.

## Starter — $49/month  
Best for individuals automating personal or small-team tasks.  
- **100** workflow runs per month
- **1** user
- Basic integrations: Slack, Email, Webhooks, Google Sheets
- Email support, **48-hour** response SLA

## Pro — $299/month  
Best for growing teams that need more integrations and API access.  
- **10,000** workflow runs per month
- Up to **10** users
- All standard integrations
- API access (1000 req/min)
- **90-day** run log retention
- Email + chat support, **8-hour** response SLA

## Enterprise — Custom pricing  
Best for organizations with security, compliance, or scale requirements.  
- Unlimited workflow runs
- Unlimited users
- All integrations + custom integrations on request
- Unlimited API access
- **365-day** run log retention
- SAML 2.0 SSO, SCIM, IP allowlist, audit log
- Dedicated account team, **1-hour** response SLA
- Custom contracts, MSAs, BAAs available

## Annual discount  
Annual billing saves 20% across all plans. Contact your account team for annual quotes on Enterprise.

# Usage and Overages  
Track your workflow run consumption and understand overage charges.

## Viewing usage  
**Settings → Billing → Usage** shows:  
- Current month's run count vs plan limit
- Daily run breakdown
- Top workflows by run count
- Projected end-of-month total

## Overage handling  
If you exceed your plan's run limit:  
- **Starter**: Overage runs are blocked. Upgrade to Pro or wait until next month.
- **Pro**: Overage runs are allowed at $0.01 per additional run, billed at the end of the month.
- **Enterprise**: Overages are negotiated per contract.

## Run limit alerts  
By default, Helix sends email alerts at 80%, 100%, and 125% of your monthly limit. Configure recipients under **Settings → Billing → Alerts**.

## What counts as a run  
A "run" is a single execution of a workflow trigger-to-completion. Failed runs count. Test runs do **not** count. Manual triggers count. Cancelled runs are pro-rated based on steps executed.

## Reducing run consumption  
If you're consistently near your limit:  
- Consolidate workflows that always run together.
- Use conditions to early-exit workflows that don't need the full pipeline.
- Switch high-frequency triggers to lower-frequency schedules.
- Upgrade to a higher plan with more headroom.

# Custom Reports  
Build and schedule custom reports on top of your workspace data.

## Creating a report  
**Analytics → Reports → New**. Define:  
- Data source (runs, workflows, audit log, users)
- Filters (date range, status, workflow)
- Grouping (by day, week, workflow, user)
- Metrics (count, sum, average, p95)

## Saving and scheduling  
Save the report and optionally schedule delivery:  
- Frequency: daily, weekly, monthly
- Recipients: any email addresses
- Format: PDF, CSV, or inline HTML

## Report templates  
Helix includes pre-built templates:  
- Weekly run volume by workflow
- Monthly cost report (Pro+)
- Failed run summary
- User activity

## Programmatic access  
Run reports via API:  
```
POST /v2/reports/{report_id}/run
```  
The response is a job ID; poll until complete.

## Plan availability

# Custom Webhooks  
Trigger Helix workflows from any service that can send an HTTP POST request.

## Creating a webhook trigger  
1. In the workflow editor, add a Webhook trigger.
2. Helix generates a unique URL: `https://hooks.helix.io/wf/<workflow-id>/<token>`.
3. Configure your external service to POST to this URL when the event occurs.

## Request format  
Helix accepts any JSON body. The body is parsed and made available as `{trigger.body}` in subsequent steps.  
Headers and query parameters are also accessible:
- `{trigger.headers}`
- `{trigger.query}`

## Authentication  
By default, webhook URLs are unauthenticated — anyone with the URL can trigger your workflow. For sensitive workflows, enable signature verification:  
1. In the trigger settings, enable **Verify signature**.
2. Helix generates a webhook secret. Copy it.
3. Configure your external service to sign requests with **HMAC-SHA256** using the secret.
4. Send the signature in the **X-Helix-Signature** header.  
Helix will reject requests with invalid or missing signatures.

## Timeouts and retries  
- Helix webhook endpoints respond within **30 seconds** of receiving a request.
- If your service expects a synchronous response, your workflow's first step's output will be returned. Otherwise, Helix returns 200 immediately and processes the workflow asynchronously.
- If Helix's endpoint is temporarily unavailable, callers should retry with backoff. We recommend **3** retries.

## Outbound webhooks  
To send a webhook from a workflow, use the **HTTP** action. You can sign outbound webhooks by computing an HMAC over the body and adding it as a header.

# OAuth Connection Flow  
Most Helix integrations use OAuth 2.0 for authentication. This page explains what happens during the connection flow and how to troubleshoot common issues.

## Connection steps  
1. **You click Connect** in Helix. Helix records a connection attempt.
2. **Helix redirects to the provider** (e.g., Google, Salesforce). The redirect includes Helix's client ID and the requested scopes.
3. **You authorize** the connection on the provider's site.
4. **Provider redirects back** to Helix with an authorization code.
5. **Helix exchanges the code** for an access token and refresh token.
6. **Helix stores credentials** in encrypted storage and marks the connection as Active.

## Token refresh  
Most providers issue access tokens that expire (usually after 1 hour). Helix uses the refresh token to obtain new access tokens automatically. You should not need to reconnect unless the refresh token itself expires (typically after 60–90 days of inactivity, depending on the provider).

## Troubleshooting  
**"Invalid scope" error during authorization**
Check that the provider account has access to the resource type you are connecting (e.g., Google Drive vs Google Workspace).  
**"Connection expired" status in Helix**
The refresh token has been revoked or expired. Click **Reconnect** to refresh.  
**Provider asks "Helix is requesting access to your account"**
Expected. Helix is requesting the scopes needed for the specific integration. We do not request scopes we don't use.  
**Connection works in Helix but actions fail with 401**
Likely a permissions issue at the provider. The connected user may have lost access to the resource. Check provider-side permissions.

Helix Slack messages use Block Kit. Each message includes:  
- Workflow name and link
- Status (succeeded / failed)
- Trigger summary
- Action buttons (Re-run, View logs, Acknowledge)

## Channel vs DM  
Notifications can go to channels (visible to all members) or DMs (private to a user). DM destinations require the recipient to have authorized the Helix Slack app.

## Threading  
To reduce channel noise, enable **Thread updates**. Subsequent updates to the same workflow run are posted as replies to the original message instead of new messages.

# Conditions and Branching  
Conditional logic lets your workflow take different paths based on data.

## Condition steps  
Insert a **Condition** step between any two steps. A condition evaluates an expression and routes the workflow to the True branch or False branch.

## Expression syntax  
Conditions support comparison operators (`==`, `!=`, `>`, `<`, `>=`, `<=`), logical operators (`and`, `or`, `not`), and string functions (`contains`, `starts_with`, `ends_with`).  
Examples:
- `{{trigger.amount}} > 1000`
- `{{trigger.email}} ends_with "@enterprise.com"`
- `{{step1.status}} == "approved" and {{trigger.priority}} != "low"`

## Branching strategies  
### Two-way branching
Standard if-else. The Condition step has two outputs: True and False.

### Multi-way branching
Chain Condition steps for if-else-if logic. Each subsequent condition is reached only if the prior one was False.

### Parallel branches
Use a **Split** step to run multiple branches simultaneously. The workflow waits for all branches to complete before continuing.

## Common patterns  
- **Approval routing**: Route to different approvers based on amount or category.
- **Customer segmentation**: Send different emails to free vs paid users.
- **Escalation**: Skip first-tier handling for high-priority items.

# Creating Workflows  
Workflows are the core of Helix. This guide covers everything you need to know about building them.

## Workflow structure  
Every workflow has exactly one trigger and one or more steps. Steps run sequentially by default but can be branched, looped, or run in parallel.

## Creating a new workflow  
From the **Workflows** page, click **New Workflow**. You will be taken to the workflow builder.

## Workflow limits  
- Maximum steps per workflow: **100**
- Maximum runtime per run: **30 minutes**
- Workflow versions retained: **50** (older versions are deleted automatically)  
If your workflow exceeds these limits, the run will be terminated and marked as failed.

## Naming conventions  
While not required, we recommend descriptive workflow names with action verbs (e.g., "Post new leads to #sales" rather than "Slack workflow"). Names are searchable in the dashboard.

## Activating workflows  
A workflow does not run until it is set to Active. Toggle the **Active** switch in the workflow editor. Inactive workflows can still be tested manually.

## Cloning workflows  
Right-click any workflow and select **Clone** to create a copy. The clone is created in Inactive state to prevent accidental duplicate runs.

# Error Handling and Retries  
When a workflow step fails, Helix automatically retries before marking the run as failed.

## Default retry behavior  
Failed steps retry **3 times** with exponential backoff:  
- 1st retry: after **1 minute**
- 2nd retry: after **5 minutes**
- 3rd retry: after **25 minutes**  
If all retries fail, the run is marked as **Failed** and the workflow's failure handler runs (if configured).

## What counts as a failure  
- Network errors (timeouts, connection refused)
- HTTP 5xx responses from integrated apps
- HTTP 429 (rate limit) responses
- Explicit step errors (e.g., a Code step throwing an exception)  
HTTP 4xx responses (except 429) are **not** retried because they typically indicate a permanent problem (bad request, unauthorized).

## Custom retry configuration  
You can override the default retry settings on individual steps:  
- **Retry count**: 0 to 5
- **Backoff strategy**: Fixed, Linear, or Exponential
- **Initial delay**: 0s to 5min

## Failure handlers  
Configure a failure handler at the workflow level under **Settings → Failure handler**. The handler can:  
- Send a Slack or email notification
- Trigger another workflow
- Write to a Failures collection for later review

## Idempotency  
Because steps may retry, your integrations should be idempotent. For HTTP calls, include an `Idempotency-Key` header to avoid duplicate side effects.

# Loops  
Loops let you process collections of data — for example, sending an email to every user in a list.

## Loop step  
Insert a **Loop** step. Connect it to a list — typically the output of a previous step that returned an array.

## Loop variables  
Inside a loop, the following variables are available:  
- `{{loop.item}}` — The current item being processed.
- `{{loop.index}}` — The current 0-based index.
- `{{loop.total}}` — The total number of items.

## Performance considerations  
Loops execute sequentially by default. For 100 items at 1 second each, that's 100 seconds. If your loop iterations are independent, use a **Parallel Loop** step to process up to 10 items concurrently.

## Limits  
- Maximum iterations per loop: 1,000
- Maximum nested loop depth: 3
- Total workflow runtime still capped at 30 minutes regardless of loop count

## Common pitfalls  
**Hitting rate limits**: If your loop calls an external API, you may hit rate limits. Add a delay step inside the loop or use parallelism cautiously.  
**Memory issues**: Very large loops accumulate state. If you don't need data from prior iterations, clear it explicitly.

# Parallel Execution  
Run independent branches of your workflow concurrently to reduce total runtime.

## Split step  
Insert a **Split** step. Each output line from the Split is a parallel branch. Branches execute simultaneously and the workflow waits for all of them to finish before continuing.

## When to use parallelism  
- Calling multiple independent APIs (e.g., enrich a contact from Clearbit and FullContact in parallel).
- Sending notifications to multiple channels.
- Aggregating data from multiple sources.

## When not to use parallelism  
- Sequential dependencies — if step B needs the output of step A, they must run sequentially.
- Rate-sensitive operations — running 10 calls in parallel can trigger rate limits faster than running them sequentially.

## Combining branches  
After parallel branches, use a **Join** step to merge their outputs. The Join exposes each branch's output as `{{branch_name.last_step.output}}`.

## Limits  
- Maximum parallel branches per Split: 10
- Maximum nested Split depth: 2

# Scheduling Workflows  
Helix supports scheduled workflows using standard 5-field cron expressions.

## Cron format  
A cron expression has 5 fields:  
```
minute (0-59)  hour (0-23)  day-of-month (1-31)  month (1-12)  day-of-week (0-6, 0=Sunday)
```

## Common patterns  
| Schedule | Cron expression |
|----------|----------------|
| Every hour | `0 * * * *` |
| Every day at 9am | `0 9 * * *` |
| Weekdays at 9am | `0 9 * * 1-5` |
| Every 15 minutes | `*/15 * * * *` |
| First of the month | `0 0 1 * *` |
| Every Sunday at midnight | `0 0 * * 0` |

## Timezone handling  
All schedules run in **UTC**. Helix does not currently support per-workflow timezones. To run at 9am in your local time, calculate the UTC offset and adjust accordingly.

## Schedule precision  
Scheduled workflows are dispatched within 60 seconds of their scheduled time. Do not rely on cron for sub-minute precision — use webhook triggers if precise timing is critical.

## Daylight saving time  
Because Helix uses UTC, DST does not affect your schedules. If your local time observes DST, your workflow's local trigger time will shift by one hour twice a year.

# Testing Workflows  
Test before you ship. Helix provides several mechanisms for validating workflows without affecting production data.

## Test mode  
In the workflow editor, click **Test**. Helix will:  
1. Prompt you for sample trigger data (or use the most recent real trigger).
2. Run every step with that data.
3. Show you the inputs and outputs of each step.  
Test runs do not count toward your monthly run quota.

## Step-level testing  
Each step has a **Test this step** button. This is useful when debugging a specific step without re-running the whole workflow.

## Test data sources  
You can provide test data via:  
- **Manual entry**: Type a JSON payload.
- **Sample data**: Use a recent real run as the input.
- **Stored fixtures**: Save commonly-used test payloads under **Settings → Test data**.

## Production safety  
By default, test runs **do** call external services. If your workflow sends emails or charges credit cards, test runs will perform those actions. To disable side effects, enable **Dry run mode** in the test panel — Helix will mock external calls and return synthesized responses.

## Continuous testing  
For Enterprise customers, Helix supports scheduled workflow tests via the API. You can set up monitoring that runs your critical workflows nightly with known inputs and alerts you if outputs drift.

# Triggers  
A trigger is the event that starts a workflow. Every workflow has exactly one trigger.

## Trigger types  
### Webhook trigger
Helix generates a unique URL for your workflow. Send a POST request to this URL to trigger a run. The request body is available as `{{trigger.body}}` in subsequent steps.

### Schedule trigger
Run a workflow on a fixed schedule using cron syntax. The format is the standard 5-field cron expression: `minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week`.  
Examples:
- `0 9 * * 1-5` — Every weekday at 9am UTC
- `*/15 * * * *` — Every 15 minutes
- `0 0 1 * *` — First day of every month  
All schedules run in UTC.

### App event trigger
Trigger when something happens in a connected app — for example, "new row in Google Sheets" or "new contact in HubSpot". Available events depend on the integration.

### Manual trigger
Run only when manually started from the dashboard or API. Useful for ad-hoc workflows.

## Trigger data  
Trigger data is available throughout your workflow via the `trigger` object. The exact shape depends on the trigger type. You can inspect the trigger payload in the Runs view.

# Workflow Versioning  
Every change to a workflow creates a new version. Helix retains the last **50 versions** of each workflow.

## How versions are created  
A new version is created when you click **Save** in the workflow editor with at least one change. Minor edits like renaming or comment changes are batched into a single version if saved within 5 minutes.

## Viewing version history  
In the workflow editor, click **Version History** in the top right. You will see a list of versions with timestamps and the user who made each change.

## Reverting to a prior version  
Click any version and select **Restore**. This creates a new version that matches the selected one — it does not delete the versions in between. Active runs are not affected; they continue using the version they started on.

## Comparing versions  
Click **Compare** to see a side-by-side diff of two versions. Added, modified, and removed steps are highlighted.

## Production vs draft  
Helix has a single live version per workflow. There is no separate "production" and "staging" environment within a workflow. To stage changes, clone the workflow and test the clone before promoting changes to the original.

## Version retention  
Versions older than the 50-version limit are deleted automatically. To preserve historical state beyond this, export the workflow as JSON via the API.

Database Failover Procedure
INTERNAL — Helix Engineering / CS Operations
OVERVIEW
This runbook describes how to manually fail over the primary Postgres database to its replica. This is a
high-impact procedure; only execute under direction of an incident commander.

Verify that the replica is healthy and replication lag is under 5 seconds. Check the replication monitoring
dashboard before proceeding.
STEP 1 — Stop writes
From the bastion: `kubectl scale deployment/api-server --replicas=0`. This stops new writes from
reaching the primary. Workflow runs in flight will fail; this is acceptable for the duration of failover.
STEP 2 — Wait for replication to catch up
Run `psql -c 'SELECT pg_last_wal_receive_lsn(), pg_last_wal_replay_lsn();'` on the replica until both
values match. This confirms all writes have replicated.
STEP 3 — Promote replica
Run `pg_ctl promote -D /var/lib/postgresql/data` on the replica. The replica is now a primary.

STEP 3 — Promote replica
Run `pg_ctl promote -D /var/lib/postgresql/data` on the replica. The replica is now a primary.
STEP 4 — Update DNS
Update the `db-primary.helix.io` DNS record to point at the new primary's IP. TTL is 60 seconds; allow
